characters: The child: a sleepy child of about three in soft pyjama-style cotton, seen from behind in most pictures.
Mama and Papa: a gentle mother in a wrapper and a father in a plain shirt.
Grandma: a smiling grandmother in a blue headscarf.
Animals: goats, a hen with chicks, bats and a sleepy cat.

narrationPlan.pace: Very slow, sing-song and soothing (about 75 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with a different voice for each character.
Pause for two seconds at each question activity.
Never rush the last page: let the ending land.

music: Slow lullaby melody with soft hum (placeholder)
culturalNotes: The compound house, mango tree and drum are common images in many Ghanaian communities, shown here as a gentle bedtime scene.
reviewQuestions: Is the language right for the stated age band and reading level?
Is anything here inaccurate, stereotyped or unsafe for children?
Do the rhymes work when read in a Ghanaian English accent?

teacherGuide.overview: A read-aloud lullaby poem. Aim for calm, not excitement.
learningGoals: Name things in a familiar evening scene.
Talk about feeling safe and calm.
beforeReading: Dim the lights or sit in a quiet circle.
whileReading: Pause before each rhyming word so children can say it.
afterReading: Let each child say goodnight to something of their own.
discussion: What sounds do you hear at night?
reflection: What is your favourite part of bedtime?

support: Use gestures to match each line.
stretch: Make up a new rhyming couplet together.

culturalNotes: The compound house, mango tree and drum are common images in many Ghanaian communities, shown here as a gentle bedtime scene.
localiseThis: Replace the animals and objects with ones from the children’s homes.
Be sensitive to children whose bedtime is not calm or who may not have a quiet home.
